full_judgment:
Mr. Hassan Ameen, J:- This petition for leave to appeal is directed against 'the judgment and order .dated 29-08-2005 passed in Criminal Miscellaneous Case 4391 of 2005 by a Division Bench of the High Court Division discharging the Rule arising out of Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Case No. 10 of 2005 corresponding' to G. R. No.48(9)2005 under Section 7/9(4)(Kha) of the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain,2000 now pending in the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal, Kishoregonj. 

 2. The case of the complainant-opposite-party, in brief, is that the accused named in the petition of complaint in collusion with each other abducted the only daughter of the complainant, Punam Roy from her lawful custody and while Punam Roy was in the control of accused petitioner the later tried to rape her. The other accused namely Prity Devnath, Bipul Devnath and Pallah Devnath are her neighbor’s and maternal uncle of accused petitioner. was married with Prity Debnath and as a result, Kajal Devnath used to visit the parents house of Prity Devnath and also to the village of the complainant usually and was acquainted with the daughter' (Punam Roy) of the complainant and intimacy was grown in between them. Being widely circulated the accused proposed to marry Punam Roy but was refused as both the accused and the victim were then student. Since the proposal Was refused, the accused made a conspiracy to abduct Punam Roy and on the date of occurrence Prity Devnath on the plea of urgent talk with Punam Roy, took her to the ferry ghat where in a trawler, Kajal Devnath and co-accused were hiding and when Punam reached near the trawler, Kajal with a knife threatened her with dire consequence and thus abducted her. The complainant made vigorous search for her daughter but having failed, met Prity Devnath, who expressed her inability and at about 12 p.m. over mobile telephone, one Adhu Mia informed the complainant that victim Punam is in the residence of Kajal Devnath and she was ultimately recovered therefrom. The victim disclosed that Kajal haying abducted her tried to rape but was not successful. The informant went to inform the matter with Bhoirab Police Station but relatives of Kajal admitted the guilt of Kajal and further proposed that they will give marriage of Kajal with Punam. This incident of abduction of Punam being humiliating to the complainant, she (complainant) waited but lastly when the complainant found that'the accused departed from promises, so made informed the Superintendent of Police on 19-12-2004. The police having failed to take appropriate action the complainant at long last filed the petition of complaint before the competent Magistrate, who sent it to the Nikli Police Station for treating it as FIR with a direction to investigate the matter. 

 3. Police took up the case and after due investigation submitted charge-sheet against the accused-petitioner under Sections 7/9(4)(Kha) of Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 (shortly the Ain) on 05‘. 03-2005. The accused-petitioner, thereafter, surrendered before the High Court Division on 27-01-2005 and obtained the direction not to harass him and thereafter, obtained bail and then moved the High Court Division for abashment of the proceeding. The High Court Division in due course heard the parities and in consideration of facts and circumstances of the case discharged the Rule holding that the police report has not yet been accepted by the Judge nor the charge has yet been framed. The petitioner thereafter has come up with the present petition for leave to appeal. 

 4. Mr. A. F. M. Mesbahuddin, the learned Senior Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that the police did not find any truth of the allegation dated 19-12-2004 made by the alleged victim before the Superintendent of Police, Kishoregonj and subsequent petition case filed by the mother of the alleged victim is after thought, false, concocted, baseless and has been made with a malafide intention for illegal gain and as such continuation of the proceedings is an abuse of process of the Court and liable to be quashed for ends of justice. 

 Regard being had to the above facts and circumstances of the case we are constrained to hold that the petition has got no substance and as such the same is dismissed.
